items.title: Sandra Gaudenzi
items.note: Credited author of The living documentary: From representing reality to co-creating reality in digital interactive documentary.
items.access: Attribution checked against linked primary record.
items.question: Which part of this work is useful to the project?

contributions.evidence: Linked primary bibliographic record.

items.branchRelationNote: Source relevance only; does not establish project involvement or concept endorsement.

items.title: Relational accountability
items.note: Research obligations arise through relationships, not just procedural approval. This is a proposed reading lens, not evidence that a pilot meets those obligations.
items.access: Proposed synthesis from connected sources; verify in close reading and project work.
items.question: To whom are you accountable before capture, during interpretation and after dissemination?

items.title: Protocol as a design condition
items.note: Community-specific protocol should shape what a system can capture, translate, retain and share. Technical settings cannot establish cultural authority.
items.access: Proposed synthesis from connected sources; verify in close reading and project work.
items.question: Which community-defined conditions must alter the system architecture?

items.title: Refusal and limits to circulation
items.note: A proposed ethical question: some material may need restricted circulation or no capture. This entry does not attribute a specific theory of refusal to Smith.
items.access: Proposed synthesis from connected sources; verify in close reading and project work.
items.question: Who can decline capture or reuse, and how does the system implement that decision?

items.title: Somaesthetic attention
items.note: Use first-person bodily attention as design material alongside observation and measurement. Felt experience needs documentation and interpretation.
items.access: Proposed synthesis from connected sources; verify in close reading and project work.
items.question: What changes in sensation or bodily awareness can participants articulate?

items.title: Textile behaviour as interaction
items.note: Treat stretch, drape, friction and wear as active design conditions. This is a project proposition to test through making.
items.access: Proposed synthesis from connected sources; verify in close reading and project work.
items.question: What does the textile contribute that a rigid sensor housing would not?

items.title: Knowing through making
items.note: Making can generate situated knowledge through material engagement. Documentation must show how an insight emerged.
items.access: Proposed synthesis from connected sources; verify in close reading and project work.
items.question: Which decision changed because of handling or testing the material?

items.title: Operational images
items.note: An image can measure, classify or trigger an action as well as represent a scene. Identify each operation in the pipeline.
items.access: Proposed synthesis from connected sources; verify in close reading and project work.
items.question: What does this image cause the system to do, and who can inspect or contest that operation?

items.title: Infrastructure as ongoing practice
items.note: A network depends on learned conventions, installed systems and maintenance. Installation alone does not establish usable infrastructure.
items.access: Proposed synthesis from connected sources; verify in close reading and project work.
items.question: Which recurring work makes the connection usable at each site?

items.title: Infrastructural promise
items.note: The promise of international connection has political and aesthetic force. Compare it with what participants can actually access.
items.access: Proposed synthesis from connected sources; verify in close reading and project work.
items.question: Whose expected future motivates this infrastructure, and whose constraints shape it?

items.title: Situated human–machine agency
items.note: Trace agency within an actual arrangement of people, interfaces, models and institutions. Avoid attributing outcomes to a machine in isolation.
items.access: Proposed synthesis from connected sources; verify in close reading and project work.
items.question: At which moments can a participant redirect, repair or stop the process?

items.title: Participation and editorial power
items.note: Navigation, contribution and editorial authority are different degrees of involvement. Interactivity does not establish shared authorship.
items.access: Proposed synthesis from connected sources; verify in close reading and project work.
items.question: Can participants change the account, or only choose a route through it?

items.title: Documentary as an evolving system
items.note: Distinguish a fixed archive with variable playback from a system changed by contributions and encounters.
items.access: Proposed synthesis from connected sources; verify in close reading and project work.
items.question: Which new encounter changes the available material or the rules of the work?

items.title: Togetherness beyond synchrony
items.note: Temporal alignment and felt togetherness require separate evidence. This concept connects signal measures with participant accounts.
items.access: Proposed synthesis from connected sources; verify in close reading and project work.
items.question: When did participants feel connected despite delay, and disconnected despite synchrony?

items.title: Selective liveness
items.note: A stable spatial trace can coexist with a limited live layer. Reduced transmission is a design option, not proven ecological benefit.
items.access: Proposed synthesis from connected sources; verify in close reading and project work.
items.question: Which live elements matter to the encounter, and how will you compare alternative designs?

items.title: Critical learning and pedagogy
items.note: Distinguish acquisition of tool skills from reflective, situated learning.
items.access: New analytical proposition introduced in source-level mapping; human assessment pending.
items.question: What changed in understanding, judgement or capacity, beyond completing the task?

items.title: Ecological literacy
items.note: Distinguish sensory engagement, ecological understanding and changes in behaviour.
items.access: New analytical proposition introduced in source-level mapping; human assessment pending.
items.question: What evidence would show learning rather than an impressive encounter?

items.title: Controllability and revision
items.note: Distinguish generating an output from steering and revising a creative process.
items.access: New analytical proposition introduced in source-level mapping; human assessment pending.
items.question: Which consequential decisions can participants revise, and at what cost?

items.title: Reconstruction, inference and evidence
items.note: Distinguish captured evidence from reconstruction and generated inference.
items.access: New analytical proposition introduced in source-level mapping; human assessment pending.
items.question: Which parts are observed, inferred or invented, and is that legible?
